claim: ContextCommandLine.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken() prefers proxy_token without ever consulting the grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken flag that gates the server path, so with the flag OFF the server sends sso_api_token while grafana-cli plugins install sends proxy_token from the same config file.
raw: The change routes `grafana-cli plugins install` through a new `ContextCommandLine.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` that prefers `proxy_token` over `sso_api_token` **without ever consulting** the `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` feature flag. Server-side `Cfg.ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` (`pkg/setting/setting.go:762`) *does* gate on that flag.

claim: The docs name the toggle `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` while the same commit registers it as `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, and since toggle names are matched literally with no warning for unknown names, an operator following the docs enables an inert flag.
raw: The docs paragraph added by this commit says: > Requires the `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` [feature toggle] to be enabled. The flag registered by the same commit is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:2253`), and `pkg/setting/setting.go:762` looks up that literal prefixed string. ... **No error or warning is emitted for the unknown toggle name**

claim: The proxy_token swap applies to the whole catch-all /api/gnet/* route including community-dashboard and template-gallery traffic, while the docs describe proxy_token as plugin-only, so operators will provision a credential narrower than the code needs.
raw: **Token swap widens beyond the documented plugin scope.** `/api/gnet/*` is a catch-all route (`pkg/api/api.go:587`), and the new `proxy_token` is attached to every request through it — including community-dashboard traffic ... The docs describe `proxy_token` as being for "plugin catalog browsing and plugin installs", so an operator will provision a plugin-scoped credential.

claim: GcomToken() has zero production callers after install_command.go switched to GrafanaComProxyAPIToken(), yet it remains on the CommandLine interface with an implementation, a mock, and a test stub that every implementor must satisfy.
raw: **`GcomToken()` is now a dead contract.** After `install_command.go:102` switched to `GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()`, `GcomToken()` has zero production callers, yet it remains on the `CommandLine` interface with an implementation (`command_line.go:101`), a mock (`command_line_mock.go:149`), and a test stub (`upgrade_command_test.go:133`). Every implementor must still satisfy it.

claim: TestIntegrationPluginRepoConfig still asserts on c.GcomToken(), but newInstallPluginOpts no longer calls it, so the only CLI-level test covering gcom-token selection no longer guards the method that actually runs.
raw: **Test now guards the abandoned path.** `TestIntegrationPluginRepoConfig` / "Should use config parameter if it is set" asserts `c.GcomToken() == "token3"`, but `newInstallPluginOpts` no longer calls `GcomToken()`. The only CLI-level test touching gcom-token selection can no longer catch a regression in the method that actually runs.

claim: ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken is a self-overwriting read-then-write that destroys the configured value, treats an OpenFeature evaluation error as "flag off" (silently downgrading to the SSO token for the process lifetime), is not idempotent across an off-to-on transition, and logs nothing about which credential ended up active.
raw: **`ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` is a self-overwriting read-then-write with no observability.** Three linked weaknesses: (a) `Client.Boolean(...)` returns the `false` default on *evaluation error*, indistinguishable from "flag is off" ... (b) not idempotent across an off→on transition ... (c) nothing logs which credential source ended up active.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: RunServer and RunTargetServer are the only production paths reaching server.Initialize, so no server entry point skips the ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken call.
raw: *Server entry points that skip the resolve ritual.* Enumerated exhaustively: `RunServer` (`cli.go:113`) and `RunTargetServer` (`target.go:99`) are the only production paths reaching `server.Initialize` / `InitializeModuleServer`. `InitializeForCLI` and `InitializeAPIServerFactory` do not construct `ProvidePluginManagementConfig` and do not serve `/api/gnet`. No production gap found.

claim: InitializeForTest initializes OpenFeature but never calls ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken, so integration-test servers would proxy to grafana.com with no Authorization header even when sso_api_token is set.
raw: *`pkg/tests/testinfra/testinfra.go:124` initializes OpenFeature but never calls `ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`* — `InitializeForTest` servers would proxy to grafana.com with no `Authorization` header even when `sso_api_token` is set. No current integration test sets `GrafanaComSSOAPIToken`, so there is no concrete victim today. Test-harness reach, out of scope at `reach=narrow`.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: ReverseProxyGnetReq guards on a non-empty token, so an unresolved token field degrades to an anonymous request rather than sending a malformed bare Bearer header.
raw: *Empty-bearer hazard* — `ReverseProxyGnetReq` guards on non-empty, so an unresolved field degrades to anonymous rather than a malformed header. Not a defect.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: passing an empty openfeature.EvaluationContext{} does not discard the global targeting key, because mergeContexts skips empty targeting keys and merges global attributes.
raw: *`openfeature.EvaluationContext{}` discarding the global targeting key* — refuted on inspection: `mergeContexts` (go-sdk v1.17.1) skips empty targeting keys and merges global attributes; `Attributes()` always returns a non-nil map.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: the flag evaluation with context.Background() cannot hang startup indefinitely because CreateHTTPClient applies a 10s default timeout.
raw: *Startup hang on flag evaluation* — `CreateHTTPClient` applies a 10s default timeout (`pkg/infra/features/client.go:47`), so `context.Background()` cannot block boot indefinitely.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: the token cannot leak to arbitrary --pluginUrl downloads because the client prefix-guards where it attaches the Authorization header; pre-existing and sound.
raw: *Token leaking to arbitrary `--pluginUrl` downloads* — `pkg/plugins/repo/client.go:240` prefix-guards correctly. Pre-existing and sound.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: the new pkg/setting to openfeature dependency edge introduces no import cycle, since pkg/setting already imported openfeature/memprovider for ParseFlag.
raw: *New `pkg/setting` → openfeature dependency edge* — `pkg/setting` already imported `openfeature`/`memprovider` for `ParseFlag`. No new cycle.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: a config reload cannot silently revert the in-place token overwrite, because no path re-invokes cfg.Load after startup.
raw: *Config-reload undoing the mutation* — no path re-invokes `cfg.Load` after startup, so the overwrite cannot be silently reverted mid-process.

claim: TestResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken sets the global skipStaticRootValidation = true at function scope without restoring it, risking cross-test pollution.
raw: *Global `skipStaticRootValidation = true` set at function scope without restoration* in `TestResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` — dismissed as pre-existing pattern, matching `TestLoadingSettings:30`. Accepted: the shuffled-run probe confirms no observable pollution.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: all three TestResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken subtests can actually fail and the memprovider DefaultVariant/Variants wiring resolves correctly rather than passing via an evaluation-error default.
raw: All three `TestResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` subtests were checked for the ability to actually fail; each distinguishes its intended branch. The memprovider `DefaultVariant`/`Variants` wiring resolves correctly rather than passing via an evaluation-error default.

claim: The new field name GrafanaComProxyAPIToken is ambiguous about which credential it ends up holding after resolution.
raw: *Field naming (`GrafanaComProxyAPIToken`)* — clear enough in context; naming is out of scope.

claim: openfeature.NewDefaultClient() allocates a new client on every call rather than reusing one.
raw: *`openfeature.NewDefaultClient()` allocating per call* — mildly inefficient, no correctness impact since clients share the provider.

claim: Checked and cleared, no defect asserted: the sso_api_token fallback is backward compatible for operators who configured only sso_api_token.
raw: *Backward compatibility of the fallback* — sound for operators on `sso_api_token` alone.
